questions.questionHtml: In the context of the pipeline, 'Predict-not-taken' is a method of branch prediction in which the hardware assumes that the next instruction to be executed will be the instruction following the branch instruction in memory. This (possible) next instruction is placed in the pipe and execution begins. If after the branch is finished executing, it is found that we really wanted to take the branch, then the (possible) next instruction that we had been executing is thrown out by the hardware, and we begin executing the correct instruction, the branch target. Consider two different 55-stage pipeline machines (IF ID EX MEM WB).(IF ID EX MEM WB). The first machine MM resolves branches in the IDID stage, uses one branch delay slot, and can fill 80%80% of the delay slots with useful instructions. The second machine NN resolves branches in the EXEX stage and uses a Predict-not-taken scheme. Assume that the cycle times of the machines are identical. Given that 35%35% of the instructions are branches, 25%25% of branches are taken, and that stalls are due to branches alone, what is the Speedup of machine MM over machine NN (up to three decimal places)? (Speedup is the ratio of machine NN running time to machine MM running time.)
